rules: Faction relations are directed edges because one institution may trust/respect another asymmetrically.
Relationship values move only from committed events known to the relevant institution.
The active diplomacy command supports conserved silver settlements, negotiated prisoner exchange, and treaties with production consumers; no treaty grants free knowledge or combat bonuses.
No global ally/enemy flag grants free knowledge, resources, office or combat bonuses.
Rivalry, feud and war are derived from current directed hostility thresholds. Political camp can modify willingness to act but never creates hostility or war by itself.
Great Tournament mediation can reduce an existing rivalry or war only through a real senior-delegation contact under safe-conduct; political camp alone never triggers reconciliation.

A real public tournament match can create bounded martial rivalry when prior hostility or cross-camp pressure colors the encounter. Rivalry still raises respect and cannot jump directly to feud or war from one match.
Positive directed obligation is a current debt. Lawful aid can consume that debt; repayment does not create a reciprocal obligation.
